entities.summary: Dong Yi was a Chinese military general of the Qin dynasty, whose leadership and strategic prowess were crucial in shaping the course of the Qin's downfall. Between 209 and 208 BC, Dong Yi, along with Zhang Han and Sima Xin, led Qin forces into battle against the various rebel groups, defeating some of them and gaining significant victories. However, they ultimately lost to rebel forces led by Xiang Yu in 207 BC at the Battle of Julu, forcing them to surrender. After the rebels overthrew the Qin dynasty in 206 BC, China was divided into the Eighteen Kingdoms, and Dong Yi's legacy would go on to influence the regional dynamics of ancient China. Dong Yi's story is a testament to the complexity and intrigue of ancient Chinese history, where the lines between loyalty, duty, and power were constantly blurred. Dong Yi's eventual surrender marked the beginning of the end of the Qin dynasty, an event that would have far-reaching consequences for the course of Chinese history.
